instructions: Calm, warm, grounded Indian-English documentary narrator. Measured pace, short pauses between sentences, quiet gravity at the start, steady confidence at the end. Never salesy, never upbeat-advert. Pronounce JeevanStock as JEE-vun-stock, Arkiv as AR-kive, Durg as Durg, Balod as Ba-lode.

launch.text: October fourth. A snake bit a nineteen-year-old woman in Panna.
The nearest centre had no anti-venom. She died on the way.
In Durg and Balod, twenty-two of forty-five rural centres got no anti-venom this year.
Meanwhile, three thousand eight hundred vials sat in the warehouse.
The medicine exists. The information doesn't reach the family.
JeevanStock is a public stock board for anti-venom and rabies vaccine.
Nurses post vial counts with a PIN. No wallet. No crypto.
Every count expires after six hours. An old number never looks new.
Families see who has stock, call ahead, and report a stock-out in two taps.
Every record lives on Arkiv. Nobody can quietly change it. Not even us.
Hindi first. Built for Chhattisgarh. Ready for every district.

demo.text: This is JeevanStock, live on the Arkiv Tiramisu testnet. Two people use it: a family after a bite, and the nurse at the health centre.
The family opens the link or scans the poster. The board opens in Hindi. One tap switches to English.
They pick snakebite. Centres with anti-venom on the shelf come first. Every status is a word, not only a colour.
Rampur shows zero vials. The family taps: not available here.
Two choices: the medicine, and what happened. No name, no phone number, no location.
The report is written to Arkiv by the server's payer wallet. The family never sees a wallet or a fee.
The receipt links to the proof: who wrote the record, when it expires, and that nobody can edit it.
Now the nurse. She signs in with her centre and a PIN.
She enters the vial counts for both medicines. One atomic batch writes both records, signed by the Rampur wallet.
Each count expires after six hours, so stale stock fades from the board on its own.
The family's report is in her inbox. She confirms it. The confirmation and a thirty-day extension go in the same batch.
The public board shows it all: stock, open reports, confirmed reports.
Verify it yourself lists every wallet, with links to the Arkiv explorer and a one-line command to read the chain directly.
And the real centres of Durg and Balod are already listed, with government shipment data, never shown as shelf stock.
